discarded_claims.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are satisfied. The driver's trace holds 23 consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, sitting 18.1 m to 29.3 m from the pickup pin at 6.1 m to 11.9 m reported accuracy, well inside the 25 m accuracy filter, running from 12:30:00. The first in-geofence fix is five seconds from the 12:29:55 arrival marker and the derived dwell_start_offset_sec is -5.0 s; there is no clock-skew finding here and POL-NS-08(a) would require more than 90 seconds before that match could be called unsafe.
discarded_claims.reason: Cites EV-GPS-00211, whose weight_multiplier is 0.39 (status IMPAIRED, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE), but is silent about the impairment and does not name the issue codes, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. The claim rests on a discounted artifact and never discloses the discount.

discarded_claims.claim: The 'arrived' marker at 12:29:55 is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05, so the waiting clock runs from the marker as recorded and needs no recomputation. At the marker the driver's device reported 18.1 m from the pin - far inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger - and the trace reports a 0.0 km/h speed alongside his stationary kerbside hold, so the 15 km/h motion trigger is not met either. Limb (iii) of POL-NS-05 applies: the marker is genuine, and it does not defeat the fee.
discarded_claims.reason: Cites EV-GPS-00211 (weight_multiplier 0.39, IMPAIRED, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) without disclosing the impairment or naming the issue codes, contrary to POL-GEN-02(1). The claim depends on readings taken from the impaired trace and treats it as clean.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I cannot settle this dispute on the record, so the SGD 4.00 no-show fee is placed ON HOLD — it is not collected from the rider and not refunded to her — and the file goes to a human reviewer.

What is not in dispute: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:29:55 and a driver cancellation at 12:38:20 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW; the GPS trace puts the vehicle about 18 m from the Blk 79 pin and stationary at that time, so the arrival marker is genuine and POL-NS-05 (false-arrival) is not engaged; and the chat log shows the driver replying to the rider's 'coming down now, 2 min' within 18 seconds, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider either. The driver's attempt to complete the pickup at 12:31 and again at 12:35 is well supported, and the rider's account of coming down to an empty kerb is not contradicted by any position fix.

The entire case turns on one fact: whether the driver held the pickup point continuously for the 300 seconds (5 minutes) that a STANDARD-zone no-show fee requires before it may be charged. The only evidence of where the vehicle actually was is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-00211, and that artifact is impaired: it contains a 168-second outage from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 — straight through the middle of the waiting window — and it carries issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, with an admissibility weight of 0.39. Before the outage and after it the vehicle sits in the same place (18–29 m from the pin at 6–12 m accuracy), but the trace cannot show whether it stayed there across those 168 seconds. Its measured in-geofence runs are 220 s and 112 s; if the driver stayed put they are one continuous ~500 s hold and the fee stands, and if he left and returned the longest continuous hold is 220 s and the fee must be refunded under POL-NS-06. Nothing in this record decides between those two readings. The chat message at 12:35:10 shows the driver was still working the pickup, but it says nothing about where he was, so it cannot carry that fact.

Because the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b), the ruling may not exceed a partial outcome and confidence is capped at 0.39 — below the platform-wide 0.70 floor — so POL-NS-09 requires escalation rather than a decision, and the discount on EV-GPS-00211 does not survive as a basis for a money ruling in either direction. The human reviewer is asked to settle the specific open question: whether the driver remained inside the pickup geofence across the 12:33:40–12:36:28 outage. If he did, the fee stands and driver compensation follows; if he did not, the fee is refunded in full.

(One evidentiary point for completeness: no clause in this category produces a referral on these facts — the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on 2 terminations in 146 trips, 1.4%.)
